messages:
michael: Noticed p99 spike on collector -> exporter path around 11:20 UTC. CPU on otel-collector went from 35% -> 85%.

emma: Seen it too. Only affects model-serving spans (huge fan-out per request). p50 stable.

raj: Any correlating change? rollouts, config, model size?

michael: No rollout. Traffic up ~15% but span count per request doubled after we added detailed token-level spans last week.

luis: That rings bells — exporter backpressure + tiny batches. Collector config excerpt:
```
exporters:
  otlp/https:
    endpoint: ingest.redwood.internal:4318
    compression: on

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/https]

processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 100
    timeout: 5s
```

emma: Metrics: exporter_queue_length skyrockets, exporter_send_duration_p99 ~ 3s, cpu_user at 82%.

olivia: We also saw high GC churn in Java exporter (our ingest endpoint). Might be heap pressure from large batch payloads.

raj: Two immediate knobs: 1) increase batch.send_batch_size to reduce per-unit overhead and fewer export calls, 2) enable sampling/aggregate metrics to reduce span cardinality.

michael: Tried increasing send_batch_size to 500 in staging — p99 dropped from 1800ms -> 420ms, CPU down 25% for collector but exporter endpoint CPU increased slightly.

luis: That's expected: shift work to exporter. We need to tune exporter concurrency and request size limits. Also consider prefix aggregation at SDK side (merge token spans into a single span per generation call).

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling update started for otel-collector/prod config (batch size -> 500) by michael at 2026-03-18T12:50:00Z :rocket:

emma: Good to push to prod canary 10% traffic. Also add exporter parallelism: set exporter.timeout and concurrency limits on ingest side.

raj: Add telemetry for span_count_per_request metric so we can correlate future regressions.

olivia: For retention/cost: if we aggregate spans client-side we reduce stored span volume and S3/DB costs. But we lose fine-grained token-level trace — tradeoff.

michael: Action items:
- canary batch size=500 @prod 10% (michael)
- exporter_ingest: add concurrency limit + increase heap to 6g (luis)
- SDK: prototype token-span aggregation flag (raj)
- add span_count_per_request metric + alert if > baseline * 1.5 (emma)

luis: I'll followup with heap/gc tuning notes and exporter GC graph.

michael: Thanks all. If canary looks good we'll roll to 100% and schedule SDK change for next sprint. :thumbsup:

emma: cc @eng-ml for awareness — this explains latency regressions some of you saw earlier.
